headline: Imposter Activity - Secret Word Speaking Game for ESL Classes
outcomes: Students practise careful description because most of the class knows the secret word but one student does not
Listening matters: students must notice vague answers, suspicious details, and overconfident guesses
The format creates repeated speaking turns without feeling like a formal presentation
Teachers get a high-energy icebreaker that works especially well for small groups and teen or adult classes
howItWorks: LessonCaptain gives most students the same secret word while one student receives an unknown role
Students take turns giving clues or answering questions without saying the secret word directly
The class listens for who sounds least informed and votes on the likely imposter
The reveal opens a short discussion about which clues were useful and which answers gave the game away
teacherUseCases: Vocabulary review where students describe a word indirectly instead of translating it
Small-group speaking practice for teens or adults who enjoy deduction games
A topic warm-up before a discussion lesson where students need to activate descriptive language

faq.q: How many students do I need for Imposter?
faq.a: Imposter needs at least three students because one student must be the hidden outsider while others know the word. It is strongest with five or more.

faq.q: Can students say the secret word?
faq.a: No. The point is to describe around the word, give clues, and sound convincing. That makes it useful for circumlocution and descriptive vocabulary.

faq.q: Is Imposter good for beginner students?
faq.a: It can work with simple topics and clear vocabulary, but it is usually best from A2 upward because students need enough language to describe without naming the word.

faq.q: Does the teacher need to prepare word cards?
faq.a: No. LessonCaptain handles the secret word and role assignment through the live student devices.

faq.q: How are secret roles delivered to students?
faq.a: No. Students join from any browser with the class link. No app or student account is required.
